issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with two parameters (int, boolean) while the problem statement and the solution expect a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int). This signature mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and can cause tests or example code that expect addGuestStudents(int) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... }. If input validation is required, implement it inside the single-parameter method rather than adding a boolean parameter, or update the problem statement and solution consistently if the boolean parameter is intentional.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define addGuestStudents as a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int), but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter name validateInput) creates confusion about the expected method signature and how students should implement the method to satisfy the exercise and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (or update the UML/problem text to explicitly require the additional boolean parameter and adjust the solution accordingly).
